#### 1. ectodermal dysplasia 10B, hypohidrotic/hair/tooth type, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.472)

Loss-of-function mutations in EDA disrupt the ectodermal development pathway, leading to hypohidrosis, abnormal teeth and hair development in X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in EDAR disrupt the same ectodermal development pathway, causing overlapping phenotypes in autosomal recessive hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia type 10B.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the genetic defects in EDA and EDAR lead to completely independent molecular pathways with no downstream convergence on shared cellular processes or gene expression programs critical for ectodermal appendage formation. _(variant: Identification of common, benign variants in both EDA and EDAR in the general population (gnomAD > 1%) that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared ectodermal development pathway disrupted by both EDA and EDAR mutations can facilitate the development of targeted therapies for the overlapping symptoms of hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, potentially through gene therapy or small molecule modulators of the pathway.
